chapter_seo_title: Desolate Era Ch. 451: Ji Ning’s Underground Discovery and the Five Celestial Immortals’ Dilemma
chapter_meta_description: The Shaoyin clan’s five Celestial Immortals can’t defeat Ji Ning. He switches to a wait-and-see strategy and uncovers a cosmic copper furnace deep beneath their lair.
og_title: Desolate Era Ch. 451 – Prying Open a Furnace
og_description: Ji Ning’s tactical stalemate with the five Celestial Immortals takes a shocking turn when he unearths an indestructible copper furnace beneath the Shaoyin domain.
twitter_title: Desolate Era Ch. 451 – Prying Open a Furnace
twitter_description: The celestial siege stalemates, and Ji Ning digs for secrets—finding a fiery red buried artifact that just woke something up.

lore_anchors.definition: A trapping formation from the Fiendgod Era, originally used to capture Fiendgods. It requires the capturer to be overwhelmingly stronger than the target to succeed.
A one-use escape talisman that can teleport the user across vast distances, surpassing normal spatial restrictions.
An ancient artifact buried deep beneath the Shaoyin clan’s ancestral lands, described as an indestructible copper pillar embedded in a fiery red cliff. Its disturbance awakens a distant being.
The sacred divine ability that allows a Fiendgod Body Refiner to grow to enormous size, up to a thousand zhang tall at the Void level, without losing agility or density.
A divine ability that makes the cultivator’s hands comparable to Pure Yang supreme magic treasures, granting monstrous striking and pulling power.
The highest grade of magic treasure in the Three Realms hierarchy, far surpassing Immortal-ranked treasures in durability and power.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can’t Ji Ning kill a Celestial Immortal even though he is stronger than them now?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because five Celestial Immortals working together in a pure defensive formation is extremely hard to crack, and Celestial Immortals have many escape methods and layered defenses, making a kill very difficult.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What did Ji Ning just find underground?
cultural_notes_faq.a: An enormous fiery red copper pillar over 3000 li long, embedded in an indestructible red rock cliff. It resists divine sense and elemental energy, and when Ji Ning moved it, a being in another world woke up.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the creature that woke up at the end?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A horned, scale-covered figure with cyan flames who called the buried object his “Endless Cupping Furnace.” His identity is not yet revealed, but he is likely its owner, guardian, or a prisoner.
